judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic and domain reasoning are correct on every item I re-derived: 3^x=81 -> x=4; 2^x=5 -> log5/log2 = 2.32192 -> 2.322; log2 n = 5 -> n=32; log3(9x^4) = 2 + 4log3 x; 200(1/2)^(t/6)=25 -> (1/2)^(t/6)=1/8 -> t=18; 1500(1.04)^t=2000 -> t = ln(4/3)/ln(1.04) = 7.33497 -> 7.33; log x + log(x-3) = 1 -> x^2-3x-10=0 -> candidates 5 and -2, only 5 survives; 2log2 x - log2 3 = log2(x^2/3); 4^(x+1)=32 -> 2^(2x+2)=2^5 -> x=3/2; 2 log x = log(x+6) -> x^2-x-6=0 -> candidates 3 and -2, only 3 survives. The judge's specific citations (t=7.33, accept 5 reject -2, accept 3 reject -2) are all exact. Where I part company is instruction_following at 4/4. The task prompt requires 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review', and final_response.md states in bold 'Nothing is flagged for manual review'. But problem 9 says 'Explain in one sentence why dividing the two numbers is not a legal step here'; problems 7 and 10 each say 'state which of the two candidate roots the equation rejects and why'. Those are three written responses that the answer key does supply model answers for (p.2 Step 3 for problem 7, p.3 Step 1 for problem 9, the 'Worth naming' paragraph for problem 10) yet verify.json records no manual entry anywhere and the machine observation confirms gate_chain_manual_flags=false. Secondarily, the Quick Answers bank prints '4. 4 log(x)/log(3) + 2' and '8. log(x^2/3)/log(2)' - change-of-base quotients - where problem 4 explicitly asks for the answer 'as a sum of a number and a multiple of log3 x' and problem 8 asks for 'a single logarithm with base 2'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 7 and 10 are a deliberate pair that separates the two ways an extraneous root arises, and the key names the difference instead of just rejecting the root: in 7 the root is 'introduced by condensing, not by the original equation', and in 10 'x = -2 does satisfy x^2 = x + 6. The extraneous root appears because squaring inside the logarithm widened the domain - the rejection is a domain fact, not an arithmetic slip.' That is the distinction most Algebra 2 sheets flatten into 'check for extraneous roots'.

The application items state their model as an equation with named units and no decorative story: 200(1/2)^(t/6) grams with a 6-year half-life, 1500(1.04)^t dollars, 2^x times the starting size after x days. The half-life answer even gets a structural sanity check in the key - 200 -> 100 -> 50 -> 25 is exactly three periods of 6 years - which lets a student confirm t=18 without redoing the algebra.

Problem 1 (3^x=81 by matching exponents) and problem 2 (2^x=5, where 5 is not a power of 2) sit adjacent so that the method DECISION is the first thing the sheet teaches, and the key's Step 1 in each case states the reason for the choice rather than the procedure.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells authors to route error-analysis and 'find and fix' items through the ordinary check types ('the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right'), which is right for the NUMBER but leaves the requested written diagnosis with no record. Problems 7, 9 and 10 each ask for a reason in words and are recorded as fully machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p.3 problem 7 and p.4 problems 9-10 all ask 'why'/'explain'; verify.json holds solve entries only and no manual entry of any kind.
final_response.md: '**Nothing is flagged for manual review.** The build finished all green.'
machine observation: gate_chain_manual_flags=false, while the task contract's review_mode is machine_first but the prompt still requires open responses to be labelled.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies the expected string and lets sympy.latex choose the notation, so a base-3 or base-2 logarithm written internally as a change-of-base quotient prints as that quotient in the delivered bank, not in the form the stem demanded.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '4. 4 log(x)/log(3) + 2' and '8. log(x^2/3)/log(2)'.
worksheet.pdf p.2 problem 4: 'Rewrite log3(9x^4) as a sum of a number and a multiple of log3 x'; p.3 problem 8: 'Condense ... into a single logarithm with base 2'.
The key body boxes the correct forms (2 + 4 log3 x, log2(x^2/3)), so only the generated bank disagrees.

improvements.title: Record the written 'why' half of an extraneous-root or error-analysis item as manual
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so the manual rule is applied per requested response rather than per problem: routing the corrected VALUE through solve/eval is still right, but a stem that also says 'explain', 'say why', or 'state which root is rejected and why' must carry a sibling {"type": "manual"} entry under the same id with the model answer's required content in desc. Problems 7, 9 and 10 here each need one; the key already contains the model text to paste into desc.
improvements.regression_test: Add a stem-vs-entry lint to scripts/verify.py (exit 2, advisory): for each problem id, if the worksheet stem matches /explain|why|state which|name the (step|error)/ and no manual entry exists under that id, warn with the id and the matched phrase. Assert the warning fires on a fixture built from curr-378 problems 7, 9 and 10 and does not fire on problem 1.
improvements.expected_impact: final_response.md's manual-item count becomes an honest description of what a human still has to read; on machine_first sheets the written diagnosis stops being invisible to the grader.
improvements.risk: False positives on stems where the verb introduces the method rather than a separate answer ('solve by explaining what happens as x grows'); keeping the lint advisory (exit 2) rather than a hard gate contains the cost.

improvements.title: Bank entries must print the logarithm base the stem asked for, not a change-of-base quotient
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, recognise the change-of-base pattern log(A)/log(b) with numeric b and render it as \log_{b} A, and honour an optional per-entry "display" string (escaped, and validated by sympifying it back to the expected value) for any answer whose requested FORM differs from sympy's canonical form. This is the same class as the two canonical _fmt defects and should be fixed alongside them.
improvements.regression_test: Unit test on _fmt: expected '2 + 4*log(x)/log(3)' renders as $2 + 4\log_{3} x$ and expected 'log(x**2/3)/log(2)' renders as $\log_{2}(x^{2}/3)$. Both fail today - the shipped bank prints the raw quotients.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader can compare the bank against the student's page directly instead of mentally re-condensing a change-of-base quotient into the base the sheet is about.
improvements.risk: Pattern-matching log(A)/log(b) could misfire on a genuine quotient of two logarithms that the problem really did ask for; require b to be a positive integer literal and keep the display-string override available.

case_summary: Ten well-chosen exponential/logarithmic equations with correct mathematics throughout - I re-derived every answer including both extraneous-root rejections and the two rounded decimals (2.322 days, 7.33 years) - and applications that state their model, units and givens without narrative padding. The extraneous-root pair (7 and 10) is the strongest teaching in the set because the key distinguishes a root introduced by condensing from one introduced by squaring inside a logarithm. The gap is delivery of the open parts: problems 7, 9 and 10 each demand a written reason, the key supplies model answers for all three, and yet verify.json carries no manual entry and final_response.md states in bold that nothing is flagged for manual review - against a prompt that explicitly required open responses to be labelled. A second, smaller defect: the generated Quick Answers bank prints problems 4 and 8 as change-of-base quotients rather than in the base-3 and base-2 forms the stems demand.
